parts.title: Into the Wilderness
parts.text: Jasper, Luz, and Kenji had planned their canoe trip for months, and now their long red canoe sat **laden** with tents, food, and rope beside a quiet northern lake. The river they would follow was famous for its **untamed** beauty, with no towns, roads, or bridges for fifty miles. Jasper, sitting in the back, would **steer**, while Luz and Kenji paddled in front.

parts.title: The Roar Ahead
parts.text: On the second morning the river began to murmur, then roar. Ahead, **rapids** foamed over jagged rocks. Kenji studied the map and frowned. "The guidebook calls this stretch **hazardous**," he said. "Fast **whitewater** like this has flipped stronger paddlers than us." They decided to **portage**, hauling the canoe and every pack along a narrow forest trail. It was a **strenuous** hike, and sweat dripped from their chins.

parts.title: Soaked
parts.text: Below the worst of the rapids, they launched again, but a hidden current caught the bow. The canoe gave a violent **lurch**, and a wave slapped over the side. For ten minutes they paddled with all the **exertion** they had left, until the water finally calmed. By sunset the three friends were **sodden** from head to toe, shivering and **bedraggled**, with hair plastered to their foreheads and mud caked on their boots.

parts.title: Around the Fire
parts.text: That night, they laughed about the day. Luz said the river had taught them to respect what they could not control. Kenji promised to check the map twice from now on. Jasper looked up at the stars and decided that being tired and wet was a fair price for such an adventure.
